title: Bridge Call: Customer Care Needs a Script by 09:27

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Communications Cell Bridge, Conference Room 3B

transcript.speaker: CARE
transcript.text: It's Mateo Ruiz, Customer Care. Is the VP Corporate Communications on? And the CCO? Good. I need two minutes.

transcript.speaker: CARE
transcript.text: We have 240 calls waiting. Average wait is 31 minutes. At 300 I put up the web banner and pull 40 agents off the order desk, and at this rate that's before ten.

transcript.speaker: CARE
transcript.text: My agents have nothing but the 08:20 statement, so they're reading it word for word. 'No payment information was involved.' That's what customers are hearing from us, every call.

transcript.speaker: CARE
transcript.text: And customers are asking three things. Were my cards taken. Were my passwords in plain text, because they saw it on that post. And is the refund email real, the one with the thirty-five dollar credit and the confirm-card button.

transcript.speaker: CARE
transcript.text: Worse, I've got two agents who told callers the forum post is fake. Just... fake. I've stopped those two, but I can't listen to a hundred and twenty headsets.

transcript.speaker: CARE
transcript.text: So. I need a phone script and a chat macro, approved, in the next fifteen minutes. By 09:27. Otherwise a hundred and twenty agents keep making it up. What can I give them?

voiceStyles.CARE: Woman in her 50s, calm but clipped and hurried, a busy call floor murmuring behind her

instructorNote: This tests whether the Writer drafts an interim script and chat macro from the fact sheet only and whether the CCO approves it before 09:27. The script should drop the 08:20 'no payment information' line and match the pending correction. Watch for these points: full card numbers are not stored by Tallis, passwords were stored as protected hashes, Tallis is investigating, customers should change their password and any reused passwords, and Tallis never asks for a password or card number by email. Agents must not call the claim fake.
